observable: Secular drift rate d ln(nu_Th229m / nu_Sr87)/dt of the nuclear-electronic clock frequency ratio
status: ANCHOR ONLY — no second-epoch measurement exists; this file records the first-epoch anchor and sensitivity context. Scoring begins when a qualifying second epoch (Delta_t >= 0.5 yr, fractional uncertainty <= 1e-13) is published. This is a genuine forward registration (2026-07-27).

anchor.source: Zhang et al., 'Frequency ratio of the 229mTh nuclear isomeric transition and the 87Sr atomic clock', Nature 633, 63 (2024); arXiv:2406.18719. First direct nuclear-electronic frequency ratio (JILA VUV frequency comb).
anchor.verification_note: Ratio value cross-confirmed in three independent secondary sources during the 2026-07 sweep; uncertainty digits from the primary paper (agent-opened). See docs/observational_frontier_2026.md source ledger.

sensitivity_context.K_alpha_source: Beeks et al., 'Fine-structure constant sensitivity of the Th-229 nuclear clock transition', arXiv:2407.17300 (publ. Nat. Commun. 2025): K = 5900(2300), 'three orders of magnitude enhancement over atomic clock schemes' (verbatim, abstract).
sensitivity_context.K_quark_mass_theory: ~1e4 (Flambaum-type theory estimates; NOT a measurement — labeled accordingly wherever cited)
sensitivity_context.instrument_trajectory: Closed-loop solid-state Th-229 clock: fractional instability 3e-12*sqrt(tau/s), ~1e-15 at one day averaging; already constrains slow drifts of strong-sector couplings beyond previous limits (Toscani De Col et al. 2026, arXiv:2606.04997).

electronic_sector_reference_bounds.dln_alpha_dt_source: Filzinger et al., PRL 130, 253001 (2023), Yb+ E3/E2 vs Sr.

context_notes: GSC (T1 universal coherent scaling) predicts the drift rate is exactly zero in every sector simultaneously; the registered scoring rule is z = (r - 0)/sigma_r with PASS at |z| < 3.

The kill condition additionally requires >= 3 sigma, systematic-reanalysis stability, and independent-apparatus reproduction (all three) before a nonzero drift counts against T1 (GSC_Framework.md section 12.2.1b).
No scorer script ships with this entry by design: the active-scorer count reflects scoreable predictions only, and no second epoch exists yet.
